title: The coskeleton term represents compatible truncated simplex families
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits], let $K$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], and let $n\geq1$. Put $V=\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}K$. There exists an $(n-1)$-coskeleton $(L,\varepsilon)$ of $V$, with $\varepsilon:\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}L\to V$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton]. For every object $W$ of $\mathcal C$, the map sending $h:W\to L_n$ to the family $(\varepsilon_k\circ h_\alpha)_\alpha$, where $h_\alpha:W\to L_k$ is $L(\alpha)\circ h$ (so the family is $(\varepsilon_k\circ L(\alpha)\circ h)_\alpha$) and $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ ranges over all maps with $k\leq n-1$, is a natural bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(W,L_n)$ to compatible families $(x_\alpha:W\to K_k)_\alpha$ satisfying $K(\psi)\circ x_\alpha=x_{\alpha\circ\psi}$ whenever $\psi:[k']\to[k]$ and $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$. For the canonical morphism $c:K\to L$, the corresponding family for $c_n$ is $(K(\alpha))_\alpha$.

source.place: Simplicial, Lemma 0183 (lemma-existence-cosk): the coskeleton cosk_{n-1} of an (n-1)-truncated simplicial object exists when the category has finite limits, with maps W -> L_n corresponding to compatible families over all order-preserving alpha : [k] -> [n], k <= n-1 (the node states this 0183 form; the earlier text named 0186). The comparison with the face tuples of 0186 is lem-weil-pbc-matching-object-proper-faces.
